$comment: The last state of the validation machinery AND ITS WIRING that somebody other than its author attacked. audit-system.py check 5g recursively hashes every .py under validation/ and .claude/hooks/, plus .claude/settings.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and the contracts the checks read. When that hash is not named inside an audit report under validation/reports/, the audit errors. Update this only when an agent from the roster has actually attacked the change and recorded the hash in its report — never to clear the error.
honest_strength: PROCESS PROMPT, not enforcement. That is the verdict of the independent audit of this very check (validation/reports/2026-09-01__system-keeper-attestation-audit.md), and it is recorded here rather than softened. It fires at ERROR and exits 1, which the version before it could not. But every satisfaction path can be taken without any attestation occurring: editing the `machinery` field silences it, and nothing in the repository detects that — only two things read this file, the check and the sentence in CLAUDE.md describing it. It raises the cost of skipping the step. It cannot make skipping impossible. Describing it as enforcement would be the exact defect it was built to catch, so it is described as what it is.
why_this_file_exists: Twice on 2026-09-01 a check was declared working by the person who wrote it and was not. C-021: 53 tokens carrying an inert alphaModifier, inspected three days earlier and cleared in writing as 'does not need re-doing' while every existing check passed. C-024: 39 warnings driven to zero in an hour, where one closure had made the citation check 96% blind — brand.md writes its citations as inline code, which the new stripping deleted — and another was closed by naming a document as its own verifier. Neither was found by the author. Both were found by dispatching an agent that had not done the work.
the_rule: If you changed the checks, someone who did not change them must attack the result before it is committed. The author is the one person who cannot perform this check, and good faith is not a substitute — every failure above was made in good faith by someone who believed the work was correct and had evidence they found convincing.
what_counts_as_an_attestation: An audit report under validation/reports/, named for an agent in the roster, produced by an agent that did NOT make the change, and CONTAINING THE CURRENT HASH. The hash requirement is not decoration: matching on filename and date was defeated three ways in a single audit — a zero-byte file passed, an 'audit-TODO-placeholder' passed, and reports written earlier the same day were reused to clear a change made after them, because attested_by was never dereferenced. The report must also verify by RUNNING and by planting the defect each check claims to catch; reading the code is what produced both false clearances in the first place.
what_was_rejected: Two versions were deleted rather than shipped. (1) A metrics-delta check that fired on a large drop in findings: it could never fire, because snapshots record end-of-session state, which is always clean. The independent audit found the cause is worse still — collect-metrics.py parses the NEWEST __system-audit.md, which is dated 2026-08-27, so recorded gate counts have been frozen for five days and read 0/0/0/0 throughout (see C-026). (2) A first hash that covered only validation/*.py and .claude/hooks/*.py, flat. It missed the wiring entirely: deleting the hooks block from settings.json killed enforcement layers 2 and 2b with every check still passing, and os.listdir being flat left validation/adapters/carbon-react.py — the script with the worst defect record in this repo — unhashed.
attested_state: Verified by fault injection, not reading: deleting the hooks block yields 2 blockers where it yielded silence; a hook under the wrong event errors; emptied permissions errors; the hash moves independently on settings.json and ci.yml; adapters/carbon-react.py is covered; and a zero-byte file, a TODO-placeholder and a reused same-day report all now fail. 24 hashed files, all git-tracked, so CI and local hash the same set.

known_open_at_attestation.$comment: Found by the attesting audit and deliberately NOT fixed in the same session. Fixing them changes the machinery, which invalidates this attestation and requires another round; doing that unattested at the end of a long session is the exact thing the rule forbids. Named here so they are inherited, not lost.
known_open_at_attestation.E-2 cheapest-bypass: The failing branch PRINTS the hash, so `audit-system.py > validation/reports/<date>__token-keeper-audit.md 2>&1` attests in one command, and a 16-byte file containing only the hash attests. The strength of an honour system is set by its cheapest bypass, and this one is cheaper and far less conspicuous than editing this file — a new report is the normal accompaniment to a machinery change. FIX: stop emitting the hash in the error branch; expose it only behind an explicit flag.
known_open_at_attestation.E-1 contract coverage: The hash covers 1 of 3 files in design-system/contracts/. component.schema.json — which all 216 component-index entries are validated against — is blind. FIX: hash design-system/contracts/*.json.
known_open_at_attestation.E-3 check 2b is defeatable: Registration is matched on the command STRING, so `gate-b.py.DISABLED`, `true # gate-b.py`, or changing matcher to `Read` all pass, and permissions {"deny": []} counts as non-empty. test-gates.py passes clean under a neutered matcher — the same proves-the-script-not-the-wiring gap one layer down. FIX: resolve the referenced path and require it to exist; require the matcher to cover Write and Edit; require a non-empty deny list.
known_open_at_attestation.E-4 unrecorded guarantees: Neither the wiring check nor the attestation mechanism appears in coverage.json, and V-004/V-005 still credit test-gates.py alone.
